core.title: Split plan artifacts that exceed 5 acceptances or mix concerns (advisory)
core.given: You are authoring or revising a plan artifact (the stack's acceptance-bearing planning artifact) and its acceptances. This is advisory guidance, not schema-enforced.
core.when: The plan artifact has more than 5 acceptances, or its statement mentions multiple dimensions, involves different actors+actions, or combines divergent gates (ALL vs ANY).
core.then: Split it into separate plan artifacts so that none exceeds 5 acceptances and none mixes dimensions, different actors+actions, or ALL/ANY gates.
prefer: Treat more than 5 acceptances as a signal of mixed concerns and split by concern.

Split along every trigger present: separate plan artifacts per dimension, per distinct actor+action pairing, and per gate type (ALL vs ANY); re-check each resulting plan artifact against all triggers.

If an over-cap plan artifact is one truth across the stack's single-truth observation tiers (gate ALL) or one coherent sequence, flag the cap-vs-keep-together conflict for review instead of silently choosing; the source does not define precedence.
avoid: Packing more than 5 acceptances into one plan artifact.
A plan-artifact statement that mentions multiple dimensions.
Mixing ALL-gated and ANY-gated acceptances in one plan artifact.
Splitting only to get under the cap while the resulting plan artifacts still mix concerns, or splitting one truth or one sequence apart.
unless: single_truth_multiple_layers: the acceptances assert the same outcome across the stack's single-truth observation tiers with gate ALL — keep together.
coherent_sequence: the acceptances are sequential steps of one process — keep together.
core.why: Beyond 5 acceptances, or mixed dimensions, different actors+actions, or divergent gates, indicate mixed concerns that should be separate plan artifacts.
evidence: Each plan artifact has at most 5 acceptances, or an over-cap keep-together plan artifact is explicitly flagged as a cap-vs-keep-together conflict.

No plan artifact exhibits a split trigger (statement mentioning multiple dimensions, different actors+actions, ALL vs ANY gates), unless a keep-together case applies (same outcome across the stack's single-truth observation tiers with gate ALL, or sequential steps of one process).
verification: Advisory disposition: this rule is planning guidance, not schema-enforced — the plan-artifact schema is not applied as a file-level gate for this rule; report findings as advisory, not blocking.

Acceptance-ceiling check: count the acceptances of each plan artifact; a count above the ceiling (maximum 5) is a finding. The check needs a per-artifact acceptance counter (a new observer); the artifact schema does not enforce the cap.

Split-trigger check: a plan artifact is flagged when its statement mentions multiple dimensions (mixed_dimensions), it involves different actors+actions (multiple_actors), or some acceptances are gated ALL while others are gated ANY (divergent_gates). Mixed dimensions and multiple actors need semantic judgement; divergent gates could be read mechanically from the acceptances' gate values.

Keep-together suppression: when the acceptances assert the same outcome across the stack's single-truth observation tiers with gate ALL (single_truth_multiple_layers) or are sequential steps of one process (coherent_sequence), split-trigger findings are suppressed. Both cases need semantic judgement.

Unresolved precedence: the source does not state whether the keep-together cases also override the acceptance ceiling. Treat both keep-together cases identically; for an over-cap plan artifact matching either case, report the ceiling finding as advisory with the keep-together case noted, rather than assigning precedence.
Aligns with the acceptance-planning convention's acceptance cap; the two statements of the ceiling must not disagree.

fires: A plan artifact is authored with more than 5 acceptances (if it also matches a keep-together case, the source does not say which wins — see the verification note on unresolved precedence).
A plan-artifact statement mentions multiple dimensions.
A plan artifact involves different actors+actions.
Some acceptances of a plan artifact are gated ALL while others are gated ANY.
doesNotFire: Split-trigger findings for a plan artifact whose acceptances assert the same outcome across the stack's single-truth observation tiers with gate ALL (single_truth_multiple_layers).
Split-trigger findings for a plan artifact whose acceptances are sequential steps of one coherent process (coherent_sequence).
Editing artifacts that are not plan artifacts.

neutralityNotes: The acceptance model itself — acceptance gates ALL/ANY, dimensions, actor+action pairs, the keep-together case names (single_truth_multiple_layers, coherent_sequence) and the ceiling value 5 — is methodology/rule data shared by every realization, so it stays in the core rather than the profile. The only stack-specific content is the plan-artifact kind and local name (profile: roles.plan_artifact.kinds/name), the single-truth observation tiers of the keep-together exception (profile: idiom.telemetry#single_truth_tiers, a proposed key — roles.layers is reserved for dependency-ordered architectural roles and must not be overloaded; Bun: UI/API/DB), the finding id desired_outcome_acceptance_count_gt_5, the desired-outcome.schema.json / #760 reference, and the local task terms 'DESIRED OUTCOME'/'product capability' (bunOnly; 'product capability' — the stack's bounded-slice unit — has no neutral task term, so it is realization-added and activation for other stacks may legitimately omit it). Fires/doesNotFire wording mirrors bun.json exactly modulo these substitutions, so the instantiated obligation is unchanged.
